kept.summary: Unbounded-range expansion is not size-capped: explicit endpoints bypass the "clamp to data extent" guarantee, enabling memory/CPU exhaustion (DoS) from a single formula, amplified to all collaborators via buildDependantsMap
kept.evidence: `resolveRange` (packages/sheets/src/model/core/coordinates.ts, new function) only substitutes the *omitted* half of an endpoint from `bounds` — explicitly written parts are passed through unclamped: `toRange({r: a.r ?? 1, c: a.c ?? 1}, {r: b.r ?? max.r, c: b.c ?? max.c})`. The new grammar (packages/sheets/antlr/Formula.g4) makes `ROW: '$'? [1-9][0-9]*` and `COL` (up to 3 letters, i.e. up to ZZZ = 18278) legal *range endpoints on their own*, so `=SUM(1:99999999)` lexes as one REFRANGE and resolves to rows 1..99,999,999 × cols 1..maxC, and `=SUM(A:ZZZ)` resolves to 18,278 columns × maxR rows. Every downstream consumer then materialises that range cell-by-cell: `toSrefs(extractReferences(...))` in MemStore.buildDependantsMap (packages/sheets/src/store/memory.ts, changed line) and three times in YorkieStore.buildDependantsMap (packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-store.ts ~565-605), plus `Arguments.iterate`'s `for (const ref of toSrefs([node.v]))` (packages/sheets/src/formula/arguments.ts). Attack: a user types one formula (or, in the collaborative YorkieStore document, any participant does) — buildDependantsMap is rebuilt on every edit and will allocate one Map/Set entry per cell of the expanded range, hanging or OOM-ing every client sharing the document. Even the fully-omitted form is cheap to weaponise: place one value at a far row (e.g. row 1,000,000) so `getUsedBounds()`/`CellIndex.bounds()` reports maxR=1,000,000, then `=SUM(A:A)` expands to a million refs per formula. I could not open the working tree (Glob/Grep returned no files in /tmp/eval-item-hRoO8Z/repo), so I could not confirm the absence of a size cap inside `toSrefs`/`fetchGridByReferences`; hence medium confidence. No cap appears anywhere in the diff, and the new docs (docs/design/sheets/formula.md) assert ranges are "clamped to the sheet's data extent", which is only true for omitted endpoints.

kept.summary: resolveRange throws a raw TypeError on a reference without ':' — safe only because the sole current caller wraps it in try/catch
kept.evidence: `resolveRange` does `const [fromStr, toStr] = srng.split(':')`; for a single ref (`'A1'`) `toStr` is `undefined` and `parsePartialRef(undefined)` dereferences `.replace` → TypeError rather than the intended `Error('Invalid Reference')`. It is exported from coordinates.ts (public surface), and the only guard today is the `try { ... } catch {}` in `expandUnboundedRanges` (packages/sheets/src/formula/formula.ts). Any future/other caller reached from user-controlled formula text gets an unhandled exception (availability). Validate that the input contains exactly one ':' and both endpoints parse.

kept.summary: Formula is reconstructed by string concatenation of lexer tokens and re-parsed, a re-serialisation step that must be lossless to be safe
kept.evidence: `expandUnboundedRanges` builds `'=' + body` by concatenating `token.text` for every token from `extractTokens` (packages/sheets/src/formula/formula.ts). The rewritten string is then fed to `extractReferences` and `evaluateWithSpill` in calculator.ts, and to `extractReferences` in both dependants-map builders. Any token whose `text` does not round-trip exactly (skipped WS, quoted sheet names, `""` escapes inside STRING) silently changes the evaluated expression relative to the stored `cell.f` — i.e. the string the user sees is not the string that is evaluated. Cross-sheet and unparsable refs are correctly left as-is via `isCrossSheetRef` + try/catch, so I found no concrete divergence; flagging the pattern only, and noting I could not read extractTokens in the working tree to verify losslessness.

kept.summary: Unbounded range expansion amplifies attacker-controlled data extent into unbounded reference enumeration (resource-exhaustion DoS across all collaborators)
kept.evidence: `resolveRange` fills an omitted endpoint from `bounds` max (`{ r: b.r ?? max.r, c: b.c ?? max.c }`), and `bounds` comes from `CellIndex.bounds()` — the min/max of *any* populated cell, with no density check and no clamp. Every consumer then materializes the range cell-by-cell: `MemStore.buildDependantsMap` and `YorkieStore.buildDependantsMap` do `toSrefs(extractReferences(expandUnboundedRanges(cell.f, bounds)))`, `calculator.ts` does `sheet.fetchGridByReferences(references)`, and `Arguments.iterate` walks `toSrefs([node.v])` calling `grid.get(ref)` per cell. Attack: a collaborator writes one cell far out (e.g. `A1048576`) plus one formula `=SUM(A:A)`; on every subsequent edit each client rebuilds the dependants map, expanding a 4-character reference into ~1e6 Set entries per formula (and `A:B` into maxR×maxC), hanging/OOMing every connected client. Before this change the cost of a range was bounded by the literal text the author typed; now it is derived from other cells' positions, which in YorkieStore come from the untrusted shared CRDT document (`this.cellIndex.bounds()` at yorkie-store.ts, `getUsedBounds`/`buildDependantsMap`) and are never validated. No cap or guard against the expanded cell count appears anywhere in the diff.

kept.summary: No magnitude clamp on parsed row/column when resolving ranges — grammar admits arbitrarily large row numbers
kept.evidence: `fragment ROW: '$'? [1-9][0-9]* ;` places no digit limit on a row, and `resolveRange` (coordinates.ts) parses it with `r: match[2] ? parseInt(match[2], 10) : null` and passes it straight to `toRange` with no upper bound / sheet-dimension check. A single short input such as `=SUM(1:99999999999999)` or `=COUNT(A1:B99999999999)` produces a Range spanning ~1e14 rows, which `toSrefs` in `buildDependantsMap` / `Arguments.iterate` then iterates one sref at a time — an effectively non-terminating loop that freezes the tab. The new `REFRANGE` alternatives (`ROW ':' ROW`, `REF ':' ROW`, …) widen the set of short inputs that reach this unvalidated path, and `resolveRange` is the natural place to clamp to the sheet's maximum dimensions but does not.

kept.summary: `expandUnboundedRanges` silently swallows all resolution errors and falls back to the raw, unexpanded formula (fail-open)
kept.evidence: `try { body += toSrng(resolveRange(token.text.toUpperCase(), resolved)); continue; } catch { /* Fall through to the original text on any parse failure. */ }` catches every throwable — including a `parsePartialRef` 'Invalid Reference' or any future validation/limit error — and emits the attacker-supplied token text unchanged into the reconstructed formula that is then evaluated. Any clamp or rejection added inside `resolveRange` would be defeated here: the malformed/oversized reference is passed through rather than rejected, and nothing is logged, so the anomaly is invisible.

kept.summary: `parsePartialRef` accepts arbitrary-length column labels, wider than the grammar it is meant to mirror
kept.evidence: `cleaned.match(/^([A-Za-z]*)([0-9]*)$/)` then `parseColumnLabel(match[1])` places no bound on label length, while the grammar caps a column at three letters (`fragment COL: '$'? [A-Za-z] [A-Za-z]? [A-Za-z]?`). `resolveRange`/`isUnboundedRange` are module-level exports, so any caller that does not come through the lexer (or a future one) can pass e.g. `AAAAAAAAAA:1`, yielding an astronomically large column index that feeds the same per-cell `toSrefs` enumeration described above. Currently only lexer-fed call sites appear in the diff, so this is hardening rather than a live vector — I could not grep the tree to confirm there is no other caller.

kept.summary: Unrequested semantic change to ALL bounded-range aggregations: `Arguments.iterate` now silently skips blank cells for every range reference, not just unbounded ones
kept.evidence: packages/sheets/src/formula/arguments.ts: `const isRange = isSrng(node.v); for (const ref of toSrefs([node.v])) { if (isRange) { const cell = grid.get(ref); if (!cell || cell.v === undefined || cell.v === '') continue; } ... }`. The issue only asks for whole-column/row/open-ended lexing + evaluation; this changes the meaning of existing formulas such as `=AVERAGE(A1:A10)` or `=COUNT`/`=MIN`/`=MAX` over a partially-empty bounded range. Worse, the design doc presents it as pre-existing behavior — docs/design/sheets/formula.md: "Blank cells inside a range contribute nothing to aggregations (`Arguments.iterate` skips them)" — so the doc does not record that a cross-cutting evaluation-semantics change was made here. If blank-skipping is genuinely required for `AVERAGE(B2:B)` = 200, that should be stated as an intentional, documented semantics change with its own note in the design doc.

kept.summary: `Store.getUsedBounds()` added as a required interface method but possibly not implemented by every Store implementation (IDBStore)
kept.evidence: packages/sheets/src/store/store.ts adds `getUsedBounds(): Promise<Range | undefined>;` to the `Store` interface (non-optional). kept.summary: The issue's literal acceptance scenario (D1–D5 formulas in one sheet) is not demonstrated and likely does not produce the stated numbers, because expansion uses whole-sheet used bounds
kept.evidence: The issue fixes a single setup (A1=10,A2=20,A3=30,B1=100,B2=200) and expects D1..D5 to yield 60/110/200/5/360 simultaneously. `resolveRange` fills omitted columns from `Store.getUsedBounds()`, which is the bounding box of *all* populated cells including the D-column formula cells. kept.summary: Newly lexable unbounded refs are not integrated with existing reference-rewriting machinery (`shiftFormula`/`shiftSref`, autofill/copy-paste adjustment)
kept.evidence: packages/sheets/src/index.ts exports `shiftSref`, `shiftFormula`, `shiftDimensionMap`, which rewrite REFERENCE tokens when rows/columns are inserted or deleted. After this grammar change, `A:A`, `1:1`, `A1:B` lex as REFERENCE tokens and will flow into those code paths, which parse endpoints with the full-ref assumption (`parseRef`). Neither the diff nor docs/design/sheets/formula.md mentions how unbounded refs survive row/column insert-delete, fill-handle, or copy/paste reference adjustment; only `extractFormulaRanges` is called out as a limitation. A partially-supported syntax that corrupts on structural edits is a fit gap for the feature.

kept.summary: Formula range highlighting silently does not support the newly accepted syntax

kept.summary: Reference parsing is re-implemented rather than reused; the lexer's REF rule is duplicated as a hand-written regex that can drift from the grammar
kept.evidence: packages/sheets/src/model/core/coordinates.ts adds `parsePartialRef` (`cleaned.match(/^([A-Za-z]*)([0-9]*)$/)`) and `isFullRef` (`/^\$?[A-Za-z]+\$?[0-9]+$/`). The file already contains `parseRef`, `parseRange`, `parseColumnLabel` and `toRange`; the new regexes restate the `COL`/`ROW` fragments just introduced in packages/sheets/antlr/Formula.g4 in a second, unrelated dialect (e.g. the regex accepts unlimited letters where COL caps at 3, and accepts a leading `0` row where ROW requires `[1-9]`). kept.summary: Expansion must be manually re-applied at every dependants-map site (1 in MemStore, 3 in YorkieStore, 1 in calculator); no shared helper, so the frontend package now duplicates evaluation-layer knowledge

kept.summary: Bounds are recomputed per formula cell by scanning the whole index, and whole-column ranges materialize the full data extent through `fetchGridByReferences`
kept.evidence: packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/calculator.ts calls `await sheet.getUsedBounds()` inside the per-cell calculation loop, and packages/sheets/src/store/cell-index.ts `bounds()` iterates every key of `rowIndex` and `colIndex` on each call (no cached/incrementally maintained min/max). For a spreadsheet engine this is a layer/approach concern worth stating in the design doc's trade-offs section, which currently discusses only correctness.

kept.summary: Blank-cell skipping in `Arguments.iterate` applies to every range-consuming function, not just aggregations, silently changing/breaking positional and blank-counting semantics
kept.evidence: arguments.ts: `const isRange = isSrng(node.v); ... if (isRange) { const cell = grid.get(ref); if (!cell || cell.v === undefined || cell.v === '') continue; }`. The skip is unconditional for all range args of all functions that go through `Arguments.iterate`, so (a) functions with positional semantics over a range (MATCH/INDEX/VLOOKUP/HLOOKUP-style, or any function relying on the yielded cell count/order matching the range shape) now see a compacted sequence with shifted indices; (b) COUNTBLANK/COUNTA-style functions over a range can no longer observe blanks and will return 0/wrong counts; (c) previously-passing bounded-range behavior (`=AVERAGE(A1:A5)` with blanks counted as 0) changes for all existing formulas. kept.summary: `resolveRange` inverts the range when the explicit `from` endpoint lies beyond the sheet's used bounds, so the expanded range silently includes cells *before* the requested start
kept.evidence: coordinates.ts `resolveRange`: `toRange({r: a.r ?? 1, ...}, {r: b.r ?? max.r, ...})`. For `=SUM(A5:A)` with bounds maxR=3, from={r:5,c:1}, to={r:3,c:1}; `toRange` normalizes to `[{3,1},{5,1}]` i.e. `A3:A5`, pulling A3 (a populated cell outside the user's intent) into the sum. kept.summary: Deleting/clearing the bottom-most or right-most populated cell shrinks the used bounds, so the rebuilt dependants map no longer contains that cell and whole-column/row formulas keep a stale value
kept.evidence: Dependants are derived from the *expanded, clamped* range: `toSrefs(extractReferences(expandUnboundedRanges(cell.f, bounds)))` (memory.ts, yorkie-store.ts). Mirror of the added test 'picks up a newly added cell beyond the prior data extent': after A10=5 the map contains A10→D1, but when A10 is cleared the map is rebuilt with maxR back to 3, so A10 is no longer a key and the edit to A10 has no dependants — `=SUM(A:A)` in D1 is never marked dirty and keeps showing 65 instead of 60. No test covers the shrink direction.

kept.summary: YorkieStore expands formulas with index-only bounds that ignore `batchOverlay`, so during a batch (e.g. paste) new cells outside the prior extent are neither summed nor registered as dependencies
kept.evidence: yorkie-store.ts `buildDependantsMap`: `const bounds = this.cellIndex.bounds();` is computed once from the index, then used for both the document-cell loop *and* the `batchOverlay` loop, even though overlay cells are explicitly the ones not yet in the document/index. `getUsedBounds()` likewise returns `this.cellIndex.bounds()` with no overlay merge, and `calculate()` uses it to clamp the formula it evaluates. kept.summary: Dropping blank cells breaks positional/array consumers (INDEX, MATCH, VLOOKUP, TRANSPOSE, spill shape)

Any consumer that relies on the yielded sequence lining up with the range's geometry — `INDEX`/`MATCH`/`VLOOKUP` offsets, `TRANSPOSE`/`SORT`/`FILTER`, and `evaluateWithSpill`'s `{ values, rows, cols }` shape used in packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/calculator.ts — will now see fewer values than `rows*cols` when the range contains blanks, producing shifted results or a shape mismatch when the spill is written back. The bypassing sites are the array/lookup functions in packages/sheets/src/formula/ (not in the diff); they need to keep receiving blanks (e.g. gate the skip on an aggregation flag) rather than being silently re-shaped.

kept.summary: `extractFormulaRanges` (highlighting) now receives REFERENCE tokens it cannot parse — the claimed "skips unbounded refs" behaviour is only in the docs
kept.evidence: docs/design/sheets/formula.md (new 'Limitations' paragraph) states "Whole-column/row highlighting (`extractFormulaRanges`) skips unbounded refs", but no change to `extractFormulaRanges` appears anywhere in the diff. Its implementation (packages/sheets/src/formula/formula.ts, documented as 'Each REFERENCE token is parsed into a Range') calls `parseRange`/`parseRef`, and `parseRef('A')` throws `Invalid Reference` (see the new `parsePartialRef` in packages/sheets/src/model/core/coordinates.ts, which exists precisely because `parseRef` cannot handle a column-only endpoint). Now that `A:A`/`1:1` lex as REFERENCE, typing `=SUM(A:A)` into the formula bar routes an unparsable token into the highlighter and can throw on every keystroke. Fix belongs in `extractFormulaRanges` (guard with `isUnboundedRange`) or its frontend caller.

kept.summary: `shiftFormula`/`shiftSref` (row/column insert-delete, copy/paste) were never taught about unbounded REFERENCE tokens
kept.evidence: packages/sheets/src/index.ts exports `shiftSref`, `shiftFormula`, `shiftDimensionMap` (visible in the export list touched by this diff). These rewrite REFERENCE tokens of stored formulas when rows/columns are inserted or deleted and when formulas are copied. They are not in the changed-files list, yet the token shape they consume just widened to include `A:A`, `1:1`, `A1:B`. If they call `parseRef`/`parseRange` on each endpoint, an insert-row on a sheet containing `=SUM(A:A)` either throws mid-mutation or writes back a corrupted formula — persisted data loss. The site needing the fix is `shiftFormula`/`shiftSref` in packages/sheets/src/formula/ (pass through unbounded refs unchanged).

kept.summary: Expansion clamps to used bounds that include the formula cell itself, creating self-references / cycles the dependency engine assumes cannot exist
kept.evidence: packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/calculator.ts expands `cell.f` against `await sheet.getUsedBounds()`, and `CellIndex.bounds()` (packages/sheets/src/store/cell-index.ts) covers *all* populated cells including the formula cells themselves. A formula placed inside the band it references — e.g. `=SUM(1:1)` in D1, or `=SUM(A:A)` in A5 — expands to a range that contains its own cell, so `buildDependantsMap` (packages/sheets/src/store/memory.ts and packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-store.ts) records the cell as its own dependant. That violates the acyclicity invariant the topological recalculation/cycle detection relies on; expect a spurious `#REF!`/cycle error or a recalculation loop. Note the new tests deliberately place every formula in column D outside rows 1-3 (packages/sheets/test/sheet/calculation.test.ts, the `=SUM(1:3)` case at r5,c4), so this case is never exercised.

kept.summary: Dependants map and grid fetch now enumerate every cell of an expanded range on every edit
kept.evidence: packages/sheets/src/store/memory.ts and packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-store.ts now wrap each formula in `expandUnboundedRanges(...)` before `toSrefs(extractReferences(...))`, and the calculator does `sheet.fetchGridByReferences(references)` on the expanded formula. `toSrefs` materialises one `Sref` per cell in the range, so a single `=SUM(A:A)` on a sheet whose used bounds are thousands of rows adds thousands of dependants-map keys, rebuilt on *every* edit (the docs note "the dependants map is rebuilt on every edit"). Callers of `toSrefs`/`fetchGridByReferences` outside the diff were written for small hand-written ranges. Worth confirming against the largest realistic sheet before shipping.

kept.summary: Cross-sheet unbounded refs are left unexpanded and flow into cross-sheet resolution paths that cannot parse them
kept.evidence: `expandUnboundedRanges` in packages/sheets/src/formula/formula.ts deliberately skips `isCrossSheetRef(token.text)`, but the grammar change (packages/sheets/antlr/Formula.g4, `REFERENCE: QUOTED_SHEET_NAME '!' REFRANGE | SHEET_NAME '!' REFRANGE`) makes `Sheet2!A:A` lex successfully for the first time. That token now reaches `Sheet.fetchGridByReferences` and the cross-sheet resolution helpers (`parseCrossSheetRef`, `getWorksheetCell` — imported in packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-store.ts), none of which are in this diff. The docs claim it "evaluate[s] to `#ERROR!`"; verify it does not instead throw out of `parseRange` and abort the whole recalculation pass.

kept.summary: `isUnboundedRange` and `resolveRange` are exported from coordinates.ts but not re-exported from the package entry point
kept.evidence: packages/sheets/src/index.ts adds only `expandUnboundedRanges` to the export list, alongside existing coordinate helpers such as `isCrossSheetRef`/`parseCrossSheetRef`. The two new public helpers in packages/sheets/src/model/core/coordinates.ts (`isUnboundedRange`, `resolveRange`) are unreachable from packages/frontend, which is the package that has to decide how to render/select an unbounded range (yorkie-store.ts already imports coordinate helpers through the entry point). Any frontend code needing to detect an unbounded ref has no supported way to do so.

kept.summary: Formula-editor helpers around REFERENCE tokens may assume a full `col+row` reference
kept.evidence: packages/sheets/test/formula/formula.test.ts imports `isReferenceInsertPosition`, `findReferenceTokenAtCursor`, `normalizeFormulaOnCommit` from packages/sheets/src/formula/formula.ts — the reference-picking / click-to-insert path used by the formula bar. None were changed, yet the REFERENCE token shape they inspect now includes `A:A`, `1:1`, `A1:B`. If any of them uppercase-and-`parseRef` the matched token (as `normalizeFormulaOnCommit` plausibly does), editing a formula containing a whole-column ref throws or silently rewrites it. Needs a read of those three functions to confirm.

kept.summary: Regenerated lexer inserts COL/ROW into the rule list — any consumer keyed on numeric token/rule indices shifts
kept.evidence: packages/sheets/antlr/FormulaLexer.ts `ruleNames` now inserts "COL", "ROW" before "REF", and packages/sheets/antlr/FormulaLexer.interp adds COL/ROW to the token-name block, shifting every subsequent rule index (the serialized ATN action index moves from `\b\x11` to `\b\x13`). Code that maps token *type numbers* rather than symbolic names — e.g. a syntax-highlighting colour table in packages/frontend keyed on raw `token.type` — would silently mis-classify. `extractTokens` uses the vocabulary so it is fine; the risk is any frontend consumer of raw token types.

kept.summary: Cross-sheet unbounded refs (`Sheet2!A:A`) are deliberately left unexpanded, but now lex as REFERENCE tokens and reach `toSrefs`, which throws `Invalid Reference` — breaking `buildDependantsMap` for the ENTIRE sheet, not just that cell. The `isCrossSheetRef(r) continue` guard in the loop body cannot help: the generator throws while producing the value, before any iteration happens.
kept.evidence: memory.ts:333 `for (const r of toSrefs(extractReferences(expandUnboundedRanges(cell.f, bounds))))` — expandUnboundedRanges skips cross-sheet (formula.ts:364), so `SHEET2!A:A` survives; toSrefs (coordinates.ts:236-243) takes the cross-sheet branch, `localRef='A:A'` contains ':', so `parseRange('A:A')` → `parseRef('A')` → throw (coordinates.ts:336-338). Same three sites in the diff's other store: yorkie-store.ts:574, :586, :602. Callers do not catch: sheet.ts:1063 (`setData`) and :1144 (`removeData`) only have `finally { endBatch() }`, so one cell containing `=SUM(Sheet2!A:A)` makes every later edit in the sheet throw.

kept.summary: `Sheet.fetchGridByReferences` calls `toSrefs` on the calculator's unexpanded cross-sheet unbounded reference and throws, aborting the whole recalculation pass instead of yielding `#ERROR!` as the design doc promises.
kept.evidence: calculator.ts:94-95 passes `extractReferences(formula)` (still containing `SHEET2!A:A`) into `sheet.fetchGridByReferences`, whose first statement is `for (const sref of toSrefs(references))` at sheet.ts:2615 → parseRange('A:A') throws. Unlike `evaluate`/`evaluateWithSpill` (formula.ts:547,569 wrap in try/catch → ErrValue.ERROR), this throw is outside any catch, so it escapes `calculate()` and kills recalculation for every remaining cell in `sorted`. Contradicts docs/design/sheets/formula.md:128-131 ("evaluate to `#ERROR!`"). Fix belongs either here or in the new calculator code (expand or drop cross-sheet unbounded refs).

kept.summary: `Sheet.buildGlobalDependantsMap` extracts references straight from raw `cell.f` with no `expandUnboundedRanges` call, so a purely LOCAL `=SUM(A:A)` throws there and breaks cross-sheet recalculation.
kept.evidence: sheet.ts:2711-2712 `const references = extractReferences(cell.f); for (const ref of toSrefs(references))` and again at sheet.ts:2736-2738 for every formula of every remote sheet. Neither was updated to expand, so `A:A` → parseRange → parseRef('A') → throw. Reached from `recalculateCrossSheetFormulas` (sheet.ts:2773-2804) whenever the sheet holds any cross-sheet formula, e.g. a cell `=SUM(A:A)+Sheet2!B1`.

kept.summary: `shiftFormula` splits a range token and calls `parseARef` on each endpoint, which throws for `A` or `1` — so inserting or deleting a row/column on a sheet containing `=SUM(A:A)` now throws mid-operation instead of shifting the formula.
kept.evidence: shifting.ts:372-374 `const [startStr, endStr] = text.split(':'); parseARef(startStr.toUpperCase())` — parseARef requires `/^(\$?)([A-Za-z]+)(\$?)(\d+)$/` and throws otherwise (coordinates.ts:366-369). Reached from shiftGrid (shifting.ts:456) ← MemStore.shiftCells (memory.ts:181) and from yorkie-worksheet-structure.ts:289. The store has already begun mutating (grid replaced/doc updated) when the throw happens, so the structural edit can land half-applied.

kept.summary: `relocateFormula` has the same unguarded `parseARef` on range endpoints, so copy/paste and autofill of any formula containing a whole-column/row range now throws.
kept.evidence: shifting.ts:183-185 `const [startStr, endStr] = text.split(':'); relocateARef(parseARef(startStr.toUpperCase()), ...)`. Callers: clipboard.ts:25 (`relocateFormula(cell.f, deltaRow, deltaCol)` while building the pasted grid) and clipboard.ts:151. Pasting `=SUM(A:A)` — a formula the new grammar now accepts and users will type — throws instead of pasting.

kept.summary: `moveFormula` and `redirectFormula` also parse range endpoints with `parseARef`, so moving rows/columns and cut-paste reference redirection throw on unbounded refs.
kept.evidence: shifting.ts:79-81 (`moveFormula`, reached from moveGrid shifting.ts:120 ← MemStore.moveCells memory.ts:233 and yorkie-worksheet-structure.ts:359) and shifting.ts:241-243 (`redirectFormula`, reached from sheet.ts:2375 `redirectFormulasForCut`, itself called at sheet.ts:2191 and :2321). Both call `parseARef` on `A` / `1`, which throws (coordinates.ts:366-369).

kept.summary: The new blank-cell skip in `Arguments.iterate` is applied to every range, not just unbounded ones, silently changing results of existing bounded-range formulas for all consumers of the shared iterator.
kept.evidence: arguments.ts:116-123 skips any blank cell whenever `isSrng(node.v)`. Unconsidered consumers: functions-logical.ts:111 (`AND`), :133 (`OR`), :174 (`XOR`) — a blank in `=AND(A1:A3)` used to yield `false` via ref2bool (arguments.ts:194) and short-circuit FALSE; it is now skipped, so the result flips to TRUE. functions-math.ts:247 (`PRODUCT`) used to return 0 for a range containing a blank, now returns the product of non-blanks; also :874 (`GCD`), :898 (`LCM`), :1392 (`SUMSQ`). functions-statistical.ts:31 (`AVERAGE` divisor), :56 (`MEDIAN`), :645/:670 (`STDEV`), :695/:720 (`VAR`), :745 (`MODE`), :1242/:1261/:1280/:1299 all change their value sets. Only MIN/MAX have tests for the new semantics (test/formula/formula.test.ts:4412-4437); the boolean and product consumers have none.

kept.summary: `YorkieStore.getUsedBounds()` reads a cell index rebuilt from document keys only, while every other read merges `batchOverlay`, so bounds can be stale inside a batch and clamp `A:A` to the wrong extent in the collaborative store.
kept.evidence: ensureIndex (yorkie-store.ts:194-204) rebuilds from `this.worksheetKeys(ws)` — document cells only — whereas getGrid explicitly consults the overlay (yorkie-store.ts:451-456) and set() only patches the index incrementally when `!this.dirty` (yorkie-store.ts:266-273). So after any dirty-invalidation during an open batch (paste/multi-cell edit), `bounds()` at :567 and :616 omits overlay-written cells and still counts overlay-deleted ones, and the calculator (calculator.ts:90-93) expands `A:A` against that stale extent.

kept.summary: `calculate()` now awaits `getUsedBounds()` once per formula cell, and the store implementations recompute it by scanning the whole index each time — a new O(formula cells × populated cells) cost on every recalculation.
kept.evidence: calculator.ts:90-93 calls `await sheet.getUsedBounds()` inside the `for (const sref of sorted)` loop; sheet.ts:2604-2606 delegates to the store; yorkie-store.ts:615-617 runs `ensureIndex()` plus `cellIndex.bounds()`, which iterates every key of rowIndex and colIndex (cell-index.ts:128-152). The value cannot change during the loop, so hoisting it out would remove the regression.

kept.summary: Formula-editor token highlighting now colours bare `A:A`/`1:1` as references, but the range-highlight path can skip them, leaving the two consumers inconsistent.
kept.evidence: cellinput.ts:336-341 and formulabar.ts:191-194 colour every REFERENCE token by index (`refIndex++`), while extractFormulaRanges (formula.ts:414-417) returns nothing for an unbounded ref when no bounds are supplied — so the reference-colour index and the highlighted-range list can fall out of sync for formulas mixing `A:A` with ordinary refs.
